## Summary

The wrap revises Eisman's rate threshold, reviews Treasury buybacks, questions Tesla valuation and compares bullish and bearish AI financing interpretations. He preserves a conditional warning that OpenAI failure within a year would cause a major correction, while acknowledging competition could ultimately benefit users and suppliers. The subsequent Fed hike supports his narrow expectation that political threats would not prevent policy action. Treasury buybacks are officially liquidity operations, and the Qualcomm warrant-value inference requires a proper valuation.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

<a id="youtube-XYD6kWTygho-c002"></a>
### 002. Treasury's small buybacks cannot sustainably lower long yields and resemble taking over a QE role that the Fed is leaving.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 3:42-5:31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XYD6kWTygho&t=222s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The announced scale is small, but the official program is liquidity support financed through Treasury cash/debt management, not reserve-creating Fed QE. Subsequent yield moves alone do not isolate its impact.

Assessment test: Compare purpose, financing, net duration supply and liquidity outcomes against a counterfactual.

- [Treasury Announces Increased Sizes of Nominal Long-End Liquidity Support Buybacks](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0607) (2026-08-19): The official stated purpose of larger long-end buybacks is liquidity support; the announcement doubles the per-operation maximum from $2 billion to at least $4 billion effective September 9.
